97f512db92.headline: GTA 6 Car Alarms: How to Steal Cars Without Alerting Cops
97f512db92.full_caption:
Car theft in Leonida isn't as simple as it used to be. 🚗

Many cars are alarmed, and breaking into one early on can alert the police and nearby pedestrians. The answer is the Slim Jim, a tool that gets you into standard cars quietly. Swipe for how it works and what to do before you have it.

How are you handling alarmed cars so far?

Source: VideoGamesChronicle

#GTA6 #GrandTheftAutoVI #GTAVI #Leonida #RockstarGames #GTA6Tips #GTA6Guide #GamingTips #VideoGames #GTA
97f512db92.alt_text: Graphic with the headline about how to steal alarmed cars in GTA 6 without alerting the police, labelled Tips & Tricks.

slides.title: Alarms are everywhere
slides.text: Many of the cars you can steal in Leonida are alarmed. Breaking into one early in the game alerts the police and the pedestrians around you.

slides.title: The Slim Jim fix
slides.text: A Slim Jim lets you get into standard cars without smashing the window or carjacking anyone. That means you can steal them without alerting the police.

slides.title: Not for supercars
slides.text: The Slim Jim only works on standard cars. Supercars and Hypercars need a later-game tool, and key cloning comes much further into the story.

slides.title: Before you get it
slides.text: You get the Slim Jim in chapter two, around 10 hours in. Until then, try late at night when traffic is light and grab a car heading for the highway. Cops are less likely to chase you there.

b887488c6c.headline: GTA 6 Personal Vehicles: How to Register, Store and Recover Your Ride
b887488c6c.full_caption:
Your ride just got a safety net. 🚗 In GTA 6, a Personal Vehicle is one you've paid to register, and if it's wrecked, the ScooterBros app can bring it back for a fee. Unowned cars get no such deal, and anything in their trunk is lost if they're destroyed. Swipe for how to register, store and recover your wheels.

Which car are you registering first?

Source: GamesRadar+

#GTA6 #GTAVI #GrandTheftAutoVI #Leonida #RockstarGames #GTA6Guide #GTA6Tips #PersonalVehicle #ScooterBros #GamingNews
b887488c6c.alt_text: Graphic with the headline 'GTA 6 Personal Vehicles: How to Register, Store and Recover Your Ride' and a GUIDE label.

slides.title: What is a Personal Vehicle?
slides.text: It's a car or bike you're legally registered to ride. Its location is always marked on the map, under the Personal tab of the Index. Its trunk lets you manage your loadout, change outfits and store stash bags.

slides.title: How to register one
slides.text: Drive an unowned vehicle to a Pay 'n' Spray and pay the fee, which depends on the make and model. Extra registered vehicles need extra garage space. ScooterBros can summon any of them for a fee.

slides.title: Unowned vehicles and wrecks
slides.text: You can steal almost any car, but unowned ones can't be recovered once destroyed, and their trunk contents are lost. Park them outside your safehouse or in a garage to keep them safe.

slides.title: Impounded? Here's the fix
slides.text: Dumping your car can clear Vehicle Heat, but cops will likely impound it. ScooterBros can fetch it for a hefty fee, though stash bags in the trunk may be lost. Or find it via the Personal section and steal it back.

b0dd9d0bd0.headline: GTA 6 Weapon Ownership: How to Keep Your Favorite Guns
b0dd9d0bd0.full_caption:
Lost your favorite rifle in GTA 6? Weapon ownership is probably why. 🔫

Guns you buy or get from a mission are yours to keep. Guns grabbed off enemies or from the world are only temporary, and you lose them if you're Wasted or Busted. Swipe for the full breakdown.

Which gun would you never leave behind?

Source: GamesRadar

#GTA6 #GTAVI #GrandTheftAutoVI #RockstarGames #Leonida #JasonAndLucia #GTA6Tips #GTA6Guide #AmmuNation #Gaming
b0dd9d0bd0.alt_text: Graphic with the headline 'GTA 6 Weapon Ownership: How to Keep Your Favorite Guns' in The Leonida Daily style.

slides.title: Owned vs unowned weapons
slides.text: GTA 6 splits guns into two groups. Owned weapons are bought at Ammu-Nation or given to you by a character in a mission. Everything else you pick up is unowned.

slides.title: Keeping your owned guns
slides.text: Buy a weapon with Pocket Cash or BuckMe and both Jason and Lucia get a copy. Each of them has to modify and equip it separately. Dropped owned guns can be recovered from your car's trunk or an Ammu-Nation locker.

slides.title: Unowned guns don't last
slides.text: Weapons dropped by enemies or found lying around can't be recovered or modified. If you get Wasted or Busted, they're gone for good.

slides.title: Unique variants and new stock
slides.text: Look for a golden gun icon on the minimap to find Unique Weapon Variants. They can't be modified, but they unlock permanently for both characters. Buying more guns also expands Ammu-Nation's stock.

4e62150627.headline: Fastest Ways to Make Cash in GTA 6
4e62150627.full_caption:
Need cash in Leonida? Crime pays, but it comes with heat. 💰

GamesRadar+ says risky crime is the quickest way to fill your Personal Cash and BuckMe Checking Account. Muggings, store holdups, car theft and big robberies are all on the table. Swipe for the breakdown.

What's your go-to money maker so far?

Source: GamesRadar+

#GTA6 #GTAVI #GrandTheftAutoVI #RockstarGames #Leonida #GTA6Guide #GTA6Tips #MoneyGuide #GamingTips #LuciaAndJason
4e62150627.alt_text: Graphic with the headline 'Fastest Ways to Make Cash in GTA 6' promoting a money-making guide for Grand Theft Auto VI.

slides.title: Risk = Reward
slides.text: GamesRadar+ says crime is the best way to make fast cash in GTA 6. Just keep in mind that an aggressive crime spree can have serious consequences for your criminal profile.

slides.title: Quick Street Cash
slides.text: Aim your weapon at a civilian and press Triangle / Y to demand valuables. In shops, restaurants and gas stations, aim at staff and press Square / X for the register. A winch from a Mod Shop lets you steal ATMs.

slides.title: Steal, Then Sell
slides.text: Cars in good condition can be sold at certain businesses and contacts, including Pay 'n' Spray locations. Fences who take hot cars unlock as you progress.

slides.title: Hit the Big Scores
slides.text: The Robberies section of the map index shows each target's potential score and key valuables. Bigger scores are riskier, so bring your partner along for support.

1b1008344a.headline: Rockstar: PS5 Pro Can't Hit 60 fps in GTA 6
1b1008344a.full_caption:
No 60 fps for GTA 6 on PS5 Pro, and Rockstar says that was unavoidable. 🎮

Rockstar's tech and development leads say the console's CPU isn't strong enough to run the game's complex simulation at higher frame rates. The Pro still gets visual upgrades, including ray-traced shadows and PSSR upscaling. Swipe for the details.

Would you have traded some visual detail for smoother frames, or is 30 fps fine for Leonida?

Source: PC Gamer

#GTA6 #GTAVI #RockstarGames #PS5Pro #PlayStation5 #Leonida #ViceCity #GamingNews #60fps #TheLeonidaDaily
1b1008344a.alt_text: News graphic with the headline 'Rockstar: PS5 Pro Can't Hit 60 fps in GTA 6' in The Leonida Daily style.

slides.title: 30 fps, even on PS5 Pro
slides.text: GTA 6 runs at 30 fps on consoles, and that includes the PS5 Pro. There's no 60 fps or 40 fps performance option, which is unusual for a major modern release.

slides.title: What the Pro gets instead
slides.text: Rockstar's Marc Chambers told Kotaku the base version uses ray-traced reflections and global illumination. The Pro adds ray-traced shadows and extra clarity through PSSR upscaling.

slides.title: The CPU is the bottleneck
slides.text: Chambers said the PS5 Pro's CPU is only slightly better than the base PS5's. In his words, it isn't powerful enough to run the game's complex simulation at higher frame rates.

slides.title: Rockstar: no easy way around it
slides.text: Rob Nelson told IGN a performance mode would have needed too many compromises and wouldn't have been acceptable to anyone. The technical team's reaction, he said, was basically 'have you seen it?'

queue.headline: 6 beginner tips for your first hours in Leonida
queue.full_caption:
New to Leonida? Start with these tips. 🌴

VGC's beginner guide covers stashing your cash, using the day and night cycle, and spotting enterable buildings on both maps. There's also a quick Focus Mode boost and a roadside repair option. Swipe for the essentials.

What's the first thing you did in Leonida?

Source: VGC

#GTA6 #GTAVI #GrandTheftAutoVI #Leonida #ViceCity #RockstarGames #GTA6Tips #GTA6Guide #GamingTips #BeginnersGuide
queue.alt_text: Graphic with the title '6 beginner tips for your first hours in Leonida' for a GTA 6 beginner's guide.

slides.title: Stash your cash early
slides.text: You start with no bank account, so everything is cash. Check the loose floorboards in Jason's bedroom to store money. If you die or get arrested, you lose the cash you're carrying.

slides.title: Mind the clock
slides.text: Day and night cycles are longer than in earlier games. Press up on the D-pad to see the time on your phone. Some shops close at night and police respond differently. Sleeping at Jason's house lets you change the time.

slides.title: Let the maps guide you
slides.text: On the world map, darker blue buildings can be entered and lighter blue ones can't. The minimap shows enterable doors and hidden rooms as you get close. In Focus Mode, a white door is open and a red one is alarmed.

slides.title: Quick wins
slides.text: Feed Jason's pet snake Dolores for an early Focus Mode buff. Once it's unlocked, you can call your mechanic to repair your car almost anywhere. It costs money, but it's worth it.

queue.headline: No Mission Replays in GTA 6, So Use Your Save Slots
queue.full_caption:
Plan your saves, Leonida. 💾 GTA 6 has no mission replay option, so once you finish a story mission you can't jump back into it. The game gives you 15 save slots plus an auto-save as a safety net. Rockstar also says it designed missions to be harder to fail, so you can experiment and play your own way. Swipe for the details.

Will you keep a save before every big story moment, or trust the auto-save?

Source: Eurogamer

#GTA6 #GTAVI #GrandTheftAutoVI #Rockstar #RockstarGames #Leonida #GTA #GTA6Tips #PS5 #XboxSeriesX
queue.alt_text: News graphic explaining that GTA 6 has no mission replay feature and offers 15 save slots instead.

slides.title: No mission replays
slides.text: Once you finish a story mission in GTA 6, you can't replay it. Eurogamer's reviewer confirmed this over a 100+ hour playthrough. GTA 5 did offer a Replay Mission option.

slides.title: 15 save slots instead
slides.text: You get 15 save slots plus an auto-save for when you get Busted or Wasted. Missions far outnumber slots, so save wisely. Eurogamer says big story missions are easy to spot.

slides.title: Harder to fail
slides.text: Rockstar's David Hynd says the team wanted fewer mission fails for players trying something different. Missions were built with many ways to approach them.

slides.title: Freedom over simplicity
slides.text: Hynd admits that keeping missions open is harder in such a big game, but says the freedom was worth it. Players are expected to learn the world's rules and reapply them.
